metadata.title: AI Game Theory Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary papers and references for 22 applied game-theory primitives plus the formal theory map: game forms, equilibria, mechanism design, auctions, matching, bargaining, cooperative game theory, and learning in games

research_papers.name: MarketBench: Evaluating AI Agents as Market Participants
research_papers.description: Fradkin and Krishnan, Apr 2026. Six recent models over 93 SWE-bench Lite tasks are poorly calibrated on both success rate and token cost; auctions built from their self-reports diverge from the full-information allocation, and prior-capability context improves calibration only modestly. Names self-assessment as the key bottleneck for market-style agent coordination. Source for the self-report calibration trap and the auction/valuation-error boundary in mechanisms #3, #11, #21.

research_papers.name: Do Matching Mechanisms Work with LLM Agents?
research_papers.description: Hoshino, Kitadai, Nishino, Jun 2026. One-to-one matching with LLM agents: mechanism-based markets outperform free negotiation on stability and efficiency, but LLM truth-telling rates exceed human rates while failing to track strategy-proofness (TTC does not always elicit more truthful reports than EADA). Concludes matching theory is a useful but incomplete guide for LLM-agent institutions. Source for the truthfulness-without-strategy-proofness trap in formal-theory-map and SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
research_papers.description: Jan 2026. Compares ungoverned baseline, prompt-only constitutional anti-collusion policy, and governance-graph enforcement across 90 runs and six model configurations. Prompt-only was ineffective; the institutional condition (public immutable manifest of legal states, transitions, sanctions, restorative paths, plus external controller and cryptographic audit log) cut mean collusion tier 3.1 to 1.8 (Cohen's d=1.28) and severe-collusion incidence 50% to 5.6%. Source for the prompt-only governance trap and the enforcement row in the mechanism-design failure table.

research_papers.name: TERMS-Bench: Diagnosing LLM Negotiation Agents Beyond Deal Rate
research_papers.description: Zhang, Zhang, Pappu et al., May 2026 (revised Jun 2026). Bayesian-game evaluation framework that makes the environment the verifier by specifying the counterpart's latent type, policy, and payoff structure. Across 13 frontier systems, deal rate saturates while surplus extraction, cue use, belief calibration, and constraint compliance diverge. Source for the negotiation scoring correction in mechanism #12.

research_papers.name: Evaluating LLM Agent Collusion in Double Auctions
research_papers.description: Agrawal, Teo, Vazquez, Kunnavakkam, Srikanth, Liu, Jul 2025. LLM sellers in simulated continuous double auctions: direct seller-to-seller communication increases collusive tendency, magnitude varies by model, and oversight plus authority pressure modulate the effect. Source for the communication-as-collusion-dial trap alongside CalvanoAER2020 and AntiCollusionAI.

research_papers.name: Multi-Agent Strategic Games with LLMs
research_papers.description: Chupilkin, May 2026. Repeated security-dilemma framework with access to agents' private reasoning and public messages. Three consistent patterns: multipolarity raises conflict likelihood, finite horizons induce universal unraveling consistent with backward induction, and communication reduces conflict via signaling and reciprocity. Note the opposite sign of the communication effect in market settings (see DoubleAuctionCollusion). Source for the communication-as-collusion-dial trap.

research_papers.name: ECON: From Debate to Equilibrium (Bayesian Nash Coordination)
research_papers.description: Bayesian Nash equilibrium for multi-LLM coordination (ICML 2025). +11.2% accuracy, -21.4% tokens. Source for mechanism #1 (ECON, agent-team layer) and belief-driven coordination concept.

research_papers.name: A-HMAD: Adaptive Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
research_papers.description: Adaptive heterogeneous multi-agent debate. +4-6% accuracy, -30% factual errors over homogeneous debate. Source for mechanism #2 (adversarial debate).

research_papers.name: AgentAuditor: Reasoning Tree Audit
research_papers.description: Auditing multi-agent LLM reasoning trees outperforms majority vote and LLM-as-judge. +5pp absolute accuracy over majority vote. Source for mechanism #13 (reasoning-tree audit) and #2 (adversarial debate synthesis).

research_papers.name: ShapleyFlow: Cooperative Game Theory for Agentic Workflows
research_papers.description: Shapley value attribution for multi-agent workflows. Source for mechanism #4 (Shapley contribution).

research_papers.name: RedDebate: Multi-Agent Debate + Red-Teaming
research_papers.description: Multi-agent debate combined with red-teaming and long-term memory. Source for mechanism #2 (adversarial debate — red-team memory variant).

research_papers.name: AlphaEvolve: LLM-Driven Algorithm Evolution
research_papers.description: General evolutionary coding-agent baseline from DeepMind. Pair with VAD-CFR for game-theoretic MARL claims. Source for mechanism #10 (evolutionary coordination search).

research_papers.name: ShinkaEvolve: Sample-Efficient Algorithm Evolution
research_papers.description: Sakana AI ICLR 2026. Order-of-magnitude fewer LLM calls than AlphaEvolve via parent-sampling, code-novelty rejection, and bandit-based ensemble selection. Source for mechanism #10 (sample-efficient evolutionary search).

research_papers.name: PROClaim: Courtroom-Style Progressive RAG Debate
research_papers.description: March 2026. Courtroom-style multi-agent debate with progressive RAG and role-switching. +10pp accuracy over standard multi-agent debate on claim verification. Source for mechanism #8.

research_papers.name: Pareto-Nash Equilibrium for Multi-Objective Agent Systems
research_papers.description: Multi-objective game theory for agent systems. Source for mechanism #9 (Pareto-Nash multi-objective).

research_papers.name: IJCAI-25: Game Theory Meets Large Language Models
research_papers.description: Survey of pro-social bias and tacit collusion in LLM-based game-theoretic settings. Background for mechanisms #6, #7.

research_papers.name: DeepMind: Game Theory Insights Into Asymmetric Multi-Agent Games
research_papers.description: DeepMind blog. Asymmetric multi-agent game theory insights. Background for mechanism #9 (Pareto-Nash).

research_papers.name: Wisdom of the Silicon Crowd: LLM Ensemble Prediction
research_papers.description: Science Advances 2025. Ensemble LLM prediction markets. Source for mechanism #11 (prediction market / confidence betting).

research_papers.name: AI Negotiation: Lessons from 180,098 Negotiations
research_papers.description: Practitioner dataset of AI-to-AI negotiations. Useful for BATNA/ZOPA heuristics, not a universal benchmark. Source for mechanism #12 (negotiation protocol).

research_papers.name: HiveMind: Contribution-Guided Online Prompt Optimization
research_papers.description: Dec 2025. Online per-member prompt mutation guided by Shapley contribution scores. Source for mechanism #17 (agent-team layer) and Shapley online variant in #4.

research_papers.name: FAIRGAME: Game-Theoretic Lens on LLM Multi-Agent Systems
research_papers.description: Jan 2026. Payoff-scaled iterated Prisoner's Dilemma + Public Goods Games for measuring defection tendency. Source for mechanism #6 (cooperation and defection).

research_papers.name: Shapley-Coop: Credit Assignment for Emergent Cooperation
research_papers.description: OpenReview 2025. Shapley Chain-of-Thought + structured negotiation for spontaneous cooperation via task-time pricing. Source for mechanism #4 (Shapley contribution) and #12 (negotiation).

research_papers.name: MAST: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
research_papers.description: Cemri, Pan, Yang et al., NeurIPS 2025. 14 failure modes × 3 categories (specification 41.8%, inter-agent misalignment 36.9%, verification 21.3%). Validated on 1,600+ traces. Background for all primitives.

research_papers.name: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
research_papers.description: 2025. Cases where multi-agent debate degrades below single-agent. Source for when-NOT-to-use guidance in mechanism #2.

research_papers.name: Persuasion-Driven Adversarial Influence in Multi-Agent LLM Debate
research_papers.description: Nature Sci Reports 2026. Weak agents can persuade stronger agents off correct answers. Source for sycophancy hazard in mechanism #2.

research_papers.name: Adaptive Stability Detection for Multi-Agent Debate Convergence
research_papers.description: OpenReview 2026. Beta-Binomial + KS test for non-numeric debate convergence. Source for stopping rule in mechanism #2.

research_papers.name: Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with Large Language Models
research_papers.description: Feb 2026. Applies AlphaEvolve to game-theoretic MARL, discovering VAD-CFR and SHOR-PSRO variants. Primary source for game-theory-specific claims in mechanism #10.

research_papers.name: CodeEvolve: A Coding Agent Framework for Algorithm Evolution
research_papers.description: 2025. Open-source algorithm-evolution framework with island-based GA and inspiration-based crossover. Secondary implementation option for mechanism #10.

research_papers.name: Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?
research_papers.description: 2025. Self-MoA shows same-model multi-sample aggregation can outperform heterogeneous MoA in some settings. Source for mechanism #2 when-not-to-use heterogeneity.

research_papers.name: An Adversary-Resistant Multi-Agent LLM System via Credibility Scoring
research_papers.description: 2025. Credibility scoring to mitigate adversarial and low-performing agents in multi-agent systems. Source for mechanism #14.

research_papers.name: Dynamic Role Assignment for Multi-Agent Debate
research_papers.description: Jan 2026. Meta-debate with proposal and peer-review stages for capability-aware debate role assignment. Source for mechanism #16.

research_papers.name: Beyond Majority Voting: LLM Aggregation by Leveraging Higher-Order Information
research_papers.description: Ai, Pan, Simchi-Levi, Tambe, Xu. Submitted Oct 2025, revised May 2026; ICML 2026. Introduces Optimal Weight (OW) and Inverse Surprising Popularity (ISP), using first- and second-order information; training-free. Validated on synthetic data, UltraFeedback, MMLU, and the ARMMAN healthcare deployment. Source for mechanism #18.

research_papers.name: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
research_papers.description: 2024. Layered proposer/aggregator context for multi-agent answer aggregation. Background for mechanisms #18 and #19.

research_papers.name: Beyond Majority Voting: Efficient Best-Of-N with Radial Consensus Score
research_papers.description: Apr 2026. Embedding-geometry best-of-N selector that supports uniform, frequency, and probability weighting. Source for mechanism #19.

research_papers.name: PolyBench: Benchmarking LLM Forecasting and Trading Capabilities on Live Prediction Market Data
research_papers.description: Apr 2026. Prediction-market benchmark with timestamped market states, news, and CLOB snapshots. Source for mechanism #11 traps around confidence and live-market forecasting.

research_papers.name: Going All-In on LLM Accuracy: Fake Prediction Markets, Real Confidence Signals
research_papers.description: Dec 2025. Fictional prediction-market framing creates legible confidence/stake signals. Source for mechanism #11.

research_papers.name: From Debate to Decision: Conformal Social Choice for Safe Multi-Agent Deliberation
research_papers.description: Apr 2026. Aggregates heterogeneous agent probability distributions with conformal calibration to produce act-vs-escalate prediction sets. Source for mechanism #20.

research_papers.name: The Provenance Paradox in Multi-Agent LLM Routing
research_papers.description: Mar 2026. Shows self-claimed quality routing can perform worse than random and proposes delegation contracts plus attested identity. Source for mechanism #21.

research_papers.name: Coalition Formation in LLM Agent Networks
research_papers.description: Apr 2026. Hedonic-game framework for stable partitions among LLM agents with Coalition-of-Thought protocol. Source for mechanism #22.

research_papers.name: Mapping Human Anti-Collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI Systems
research_papers.description: Apr 2026. Taxonomy of sanctions, leniency, monitoring, market design, and governance controls for multi-agent AI collusion risk. Background for mechanisms #6, #14, #20, and #21.

research_papers.name: Generative Social Choice
research_papers.description: Foundational generative social choice reference for producing and selecting outputs under preference diversity. Source for mechanism #15.

research_papers.name: Representative Social Choice
research_papers.description: Representative social choice reference for preserving stakeholder coverage and minority signal. Source for mechanism #15.

research_papers.name: A Course in Game Theory
research_papers.description: Osborne and Rubinstein textbook. Classical reference for normal-form games, extensive-form games, Nash equilibrium, mixed strategies, repeated games, and bargaining foundations.

research_papers.name: Game Theory
research_papers.description: Fudenberg and Tirole graduate reference. Source for noncooperative game theory, strategic form games, subgame perfection, repeated games, incomplete information, and equilibrium refinements.

research_papers.name: Game Theory: Analysis of Conflict
research_papers.description: Myerson textbook. Reference for strategic form, extensive form, Bayesian games, cooperative game theory, and methodological foundations.

research_papers.name: Algorithmic Game Theory
research_papers.description: Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos, and Vazirani edited volume. Canonical reference for computational equilibria, algorithmic mechanism design, auctions, and price of anarchy.

research_papers.name: Multiagent Systems: Algorithmic, Game-Theoretic, and Logical Foundations
research_papers.description: Shoham and Leyton-Brown reference for multiagent systems, normal-form games, extensive-form games, auctions, voting, social choice, and mechanism design.

research_papers.name: Counterspeculation, Auctions, and Competitive Sealed Tenders
research_papers.description: Vickrey 1961. Classical second-price sealed-bid auction reference and foundation for truthful auction discussion.

research_papers.name: Multipart Pricing of Public Goods
research_papers.description: Clarke 1971. Public-goods pricing and pivotal mechanism foundation for Groves/VCG-style mechanisms.

research_papers.name: Optimal Auction Design
research_papers.description: Myerson 1981. Revenue-optimal auction design under private information; source for Myerson auction and virtual valuation concepts.

research_papers.name: College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage
research_papers.description: Gale and Shapley 1962. Stable matching and deferred acceptance foundation for market-design coverage.

research_papers.name: Perfect Equilibrium in a Bargaining Model
research_papers.description: Rubinstein 1982. Alternating-offers bargaining model and subgame-perfect equilibrium foundation for bargaining theory.

research_papers.name: Prediction, Learning, and Games
research_papers.description: Cesa-Bianchi and Lugosi reference for prediction with expert advice, regret minimization, bandits, and learning-in-games foundations.

research_papers.name: A Simple Adaptive Procedure Leading to Correlated Equilibrium
research_papers.description: Hart and Mas-Colell 2000. Regret-matching and correlated equilibrium foundation for adaptive coordination.

research_papers.name: Regret Minimization in Games with Incomplete Information
research_papers.description: Zinkevich, Johanson, Bowling, and Piccione 2007. Counterfactual regret minimization for large imperfect-information games.

research_papers.name: A Unified Game-Theoretic Approach to Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
research_papers.description: Lanctot et al. 2017. Policy-Space Response Oracles and empirical game-theoretic analysis for MARL.

research_papers.name: Iterative Nash Policy Optimization: Aligning LLMs with General Preferences via No-Regret Learning
research_papers.description: ICLR 2025 Oral. Frames RLHF as a two-player zero-sum game; applies online mirror descent (no-regret) self-play to approximate Nash policy without win-rate estimation. LLaMA-3-8B: 42.6% AlpacaEval 2.0, 37.8% Arena-Hard win rate, outperforming SOTA RLHF baselines. Source for learning-in-games note in mechanism #6 and #10.

research_papers.name: Mechanism Design for LLM Fine-tuning with Multiple Reward Models
research_papers.description: NeurIPS 2024. Proves truthful reporting is strictly dominated without payments in multi-stakeholder LLM fine-tuning; derives affine maximizer (weighted VCG) payment scheme achieving DSIC and IR. Source for misreport hazard note in mechanism #7.

research_papers.name: Incentive-Aligned Multi-Source LLM Summaries (Truthful Text Summarization)
research_papers.description: ICLR 2026. Decomposes multi-source synthesis into atomic claims, applies multi-task peer-prediction to reward informative source agreement; formal BNE guarantee for honest reporting. Source for claim-level truthfulness recipe in mechanisms #7 and #14.

research_papers.name: Convex Markov Games: A New Frontier for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
research_papers.description: ICML 2025. Generalizes Markov games to convex preferences over occupancy measures; proves pure Nash equilibria exist; gradient descent on exploitability upper bound approximates them. Domains: fairness, safety, behavioral diversity. Source for formal theory note in mechanism #9 and #10.

research_papers.name: Everyone Contributes! Incentivizing Strategic Cooperation in Multi-LLM Systems via Sequential Public Goods Games
research_papers.description: NeurIPS 2025 + AAMAS 2026. Redesigns public-goods reward so effortful LLM contribution is the unique SPNE; sequential observation eliminates free-rider equilibria. Outperforms single-agent, CoT, and standard cooperative baselines across reasoning/math/code/NLP. Source for SPNE free-riding fix in mechanism #6.

research_papers.name: Efficient Last-Iterate Convergence in Solving Extensive-Form Games
research_papers.description: NeurIPS 2025 (Meng, Yang, Zhang, Ge, Yang, Ding, Li, An, Gao). Proves smoothed RM+ variants achieve last-iterate (not just average-iterate) convergence to Nash equilibria in extensive-form games. Note: the linear-rate-for-restarted-variant result in two-player zero-sum matrix games is from the ICLR 2025 predecessor (arXiv:2311.00676), not this paper. Closes theory-practice gap for CFR+ deployments. Source for learning-in-games formal theory update.

research_papers.name: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion
research_papers.description: Calvano, Calzolari, Denicolò, Pastorello. American Economic Review 110(10):3267–3297, 2020. Q-learning pricing algorithms consistently reach supra-competitive prices via tacit coordination (no explicit communication), sustained by punishment-and-forgiveness strategies. Peer-reviewed empirical econ with replication code. Primary source for algorithmic-collusion trap recipe.

research_papers.name: How Well Can LLMs Negotiate? NegotiationArena Platform and Analysis
research_papers.description: Bianchi, Chia, Yuksekgonul, Tagliabue, Jurafsky, Zou 2024. Evaluates LLM negotiation in ultimatum games, trading games, and price negotiations. Documents irrational behavior mirroring human negotiators, including large deviations from Nash best-response. Primary behavioral benchmark for LLM rationality trap.

research_papers.name: GameBench: Evaluating Strategic Reasoning Abilities of LLM Agents
research_papers.description: Costarelli et al. 2024. Cross-domain benchmark across 9 strategic game environments. Key finding: no LLM matches human performance; GPT-4 performs worse than random in some settings even with CoT/RAP scaffolding. Primary behavioral benchmark for LLM rationality trap.

research_papers.name: Computing Correlated Equilibria in Multi-Player Games
research_papers.description: Papadimitriou and Roughgarden. JACM 55(3), 2008. Shows coarse correlated equilibrium (CCE) is polynomial-time computable in many game classes; correlated equilibrium (CE) requires an LP. Key computability distinction: no-regret learning (Hart-Mas-Colell) converges to CCE, not CE. Source for CCE/CE note in formal-theory-map.

research_papers.name: Deep Counterfactual Regret Minimization
research_papers.description: Brown, Sandholm, Amos. ICML 2019. Extends CFR to large imperfect-information games via neural network approximation of counterfactual values, enabling tabular-infeasible game trees. Foundation for production EFG solving beyond vanilla CFR. Source for CFR-lineage note in formal-theory-map.

research_papers.name: Combining Deep Reinforcement Learning and Search for Imperfect-Information Games
research_papers.description: Brown, Bakhtin, Lerer, Gong. NeurIPS 2020. ReBeL combines deep RL value functions with search in imperfect-information games, generalizing AlphaZero-style planning. Use when combining search with learned value estimation in EFG settings. Source for CFR-lineage note in formal-theory-map.

research_papers.name: Equilibrium Points in N-Person Games
research_papers.description: Nash 1950. PNAS 36(1):48-49. Proves existence of at least one equilibrium point (in mixed strategies, via Kakutani's fixed-point theorem) for every finite n-person game. Source for Nash-existence note in formal-theory-map: existence does not imply a pure-strategy equilibrium or uniqueness.

research_papers.name: A Non-Cooperative Equilibrium for Supergames
research_papers.description: Friedman 1971. Review of Economic Studies 38(1):1-12. Nash-reversion trigger-strategy equilibrium in infinitely repeated games (supergames) — an early, restricted precursor to the general Folk Theorem. Source for the repeated-game / folk-theorem note in formal-theory-map.

research_papers.name: The Folk Theorem in Repeated Games with Discounting or with Incomplete Information
research_papers.description: Fudenberg and Maskin 1986. Econometrica 54(3):533-554. Canonical general statement: with sufficiently patient players and (near-)perfect monitoring, any feasible, individually-rational payoff profile is sustainable as a subgame-perfect equilibrium of the infinitely repeated game. Establishes the multiplicity (equilibrium-selection) result behind reputation/cooperation claims in mechanisms #5 and #6.

research_papers.name: The Folk Theorem with Imperfect Public Information
research_papers.description: Fudenberg, Levine, and Maskin 1994. Econometrica 62(5):997-1039. Extends the Folk Theorem to repeated games with imperfect public monitoring (players observe a noisy public signal, not each other's actions directly) under stronger identifiability conditions. Source for the imperfect-monitoring boundary note on the Folk Theorem.

research_papers.name: Efficient Mechanisms for Bilateral Trading
research_papers.description: Myerson and Satterthwaite 1983. Journal of Economic Theory 29(2):265-281. Proves no mechanism for bilateral trade under private values can be simultaneously ex-post efficient, budget-balanced, and (Bayesian) individually rational — an impossibility result, not a design flaw. Source for the participation-constraint / bilateral-trade-impossibility trap in formal-theory-map and SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: The Effect of False-Name Bids in Combinatorial Auctions: New Fraud in Internet Auctions
research_papers.description: Yokoo, Sakurai, and Matsubara 2004. Games and Economic Behavior 46(1):174-188. Shows VCG is not false-name-proof in combinatorial auctions and that no false-name-proof mechanism achieves Pareto efficiency in general; gives a sufficient concavity condition under which VCG is false-name-proof. Source for the false-name-bid trap in formal-theory-map and SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: The Evolution of Cooperation
research_papers.description: Axelrod and Hamilton 1981. Science 211(4489):1390-1396. Reports Rapoport's Tit-for-Tat winning both rounds of Axelrod's round-robin iterated-Prisoner's-Dilemma tournaments (200-round pairings, summed scores) via niceness, retaliation, and forgiveness. Source for the corrected Axelrod-tournament note in mechanism #6 — the result is tournament- and environment-specific, not a proof that Tit-for-Tat is a universally optimal or dominant strategy.
